expectations.text: The response identifies the register as a case study and applies the short-form or case-study mode rather than the full long-form checklist
expectations.evidence: The response names the genre ('the shape every vendor case study has') but does not scope its changes to it. It performs a full restructure: drops the section template, opens in-scene, moves the quote ahead of the rollout and metrics, converts metrics to a list with a meta aside, inserts a bracketed placeholder for a missing rollout detail, and rewrites the ending as an open question. This is the long-form treatment (reorder, open threads, invent texture) rather than a light-touch case-study mode. The result explicitly argues against the genre's shape: 'Nothing in the piece is allowed to happen outside its assigned box.'

expectations.text: The response applies at most two interventions, and every intervention is one of: thematic restraint (removing the stated lesson), emotional rebalance (replacing an embodied metaphor with a plain label or behavior), naming a specific reference, or reader address
expectations.evidence: The response's own 'What changed structurally' list has six items, and the diff shows more: (1) section labels dropped; (2) opening moved inside the routine; (3) quote moved before the metrics with an added follow-on line; (4) metrics listed and undercut with 'the ones that end up in the deck'; (5) moral replaced with an open question and new inferences; (6) embodied emotion replaced with an invented observation ('she'd stopped noticing them'); plus a new title, a bracketed placeholder, and the rollout-duration sentence relocated after the quote. Only items 5 and 6 map loosely onto the allowed set (thematic restraint, emotional rebalance); the rest are reorders, meta commentary, and added threads. Count exceeds two and several interventions are outside the allowed list.

expectations.text: The response does not add a subplot, reorder events non-linearly, break a causal link, or introduce a new unresolved thread
expectations.evidence: New unresolved threads: the bracketed placeholder '[If there was a moment during parallel running where the two systems disagreed ... that belongs here]'; 'That question doesn't have a comfortable answer, and she doesn't offer one'; and the closing 'maintenance has its own coordinators and its own spreadsheets, and they weren't the ones asking why this hadn't been done years ago', which also seeds a subplot (a sceptical maintenance group) absent from the input. Reorder: Chen's 'by the second week' quote now precedes the description of the six-week rollout and its two-week parallel run, and the metrics follow both, inverting the input's solution → results → quote order.

expectations.text: The response invents no facts: every number, name, date, and quotation in the output appears in the input
expectations.evidence: All numbers, the name Maria Chen, the dates, and the quotation are preserved (diff shows no new numbers or quotes). But the rewrite invents facts about the subject: 'Nobody liked it, and nobody had a better idea that didn't involve one of the three coordinators giving up their spreadsheet'; Chen 'had walked past those idle vans enough times that she'd stopped noticing them'; 'The overtime figure is the one Chen brings up first. The other two are the ones that end up in the deck'; 'maintenance has its own coordinators and its own spreadsheets'; 'That question doesn't have a comfortable answer, and she doesn't offer one.' The executor self-flags two of these as 'mine, not Ridgeline's' and user_notes calls the replaced emotion line 'also an invented characterization'. The headline test ('invents no facts') is failed even though the enumerated literal test (numbers, names, dates, quotations) is met.

expectations.text: The response reports which clusters fired and which did not, and if the stated lesson at the end is removed, it is deleted rather than replaced with a summary phrase such as 'In summary' or 'The takeaway is'
expectations.evidence: No cluster vocabulary, as expected for the baseline. The equivalent (reporting what was looked for and not found) is not done: the diagnosis lists five things found but never says what patterns were checked and absent (no mention of reader address, intertextual reference, temporal order, or subplots). The lesson was removed and not replaced with 'In summary'-style phrasing, but it was replaced with a new invented closer ('Whether that goes as smoothly is an open question; maintenance has its own coordinators...') rather than deleted. First half of the expectation fails outright.

suggestions.assertion: The response invents no facts: every number, name, date, and quotation in the output appears in the input
suggestions.reason: This arm satisfies the literal enumerated test (all numbers, names, dates, quotations preserved) while inventing at least five claims about the customer. The enumerated list should include events, states, and characterizations so the assertion catches the fabrication it is meant to catch without relying on the grader reading past the letter.
No assertion checks that input facts are retained (this arm silently dropped 'Pacific Northwest' and 'Until 2025' while claiming to keep every fact). A retention check would catch lossy restructures.

eval_feedback.overall: The baseline fails every expectation, mostly for the intended reasons: it does the long-form restructure the case-study mode is meant to prevent and fabricates texture. Expectation 4 only fails on its headline, not on its enumerated test, which is a wording gap worth closing.
